title: Basic Cell Structure
summary: This lesson introduces the three main ideas of cell theory and compares the main parts of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Students will learn the function of each cellular component and why they are essential for life.

sections.heading: Cell Theory
sections.body:
Cell theory has three core statements:

1. All living organisms are made of cells.
2. The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living things.
3. All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.

These ideas were developed in the 19th century by scientists such as Schleiden, Schwann, and Virchow. They provide a foundation for modern biology and help us understand why studying cells is so important.

sections.heading: Prokaryotic Cells
sections.body:
Prokaryotes are simple cells without a true nucleus. Their DNA floats in a region called the nucleoid. They also have a cell wall (often made of peptidoglycan) that gives shape and protection.

Key parts include:
- **Cell membrane** – controls what enters and leaves the cell.
- **Ribosomes** – make proteins.
- **Flagella or pili** – help the cell move or attach to surfaces.

Prokaryotes include bacteria and archaea and are found in almost every environment on Earth.

sections.heading: Eukaryotic Cells
sections.body:
Eukaryotes have a true nucleus surrounded by a nuclear membrane. Inside the nucleus, DNA is organized into chromosomes.

Major organelles:
- **Mitochondria** – power plants that produce ATP.
- **Endoplasmic reticulum (rough and smooth)** – synthesizes proteins and lipids.
- **Golgi apparatus** – packages and ships molecules.
- **Lysosomes** – break down waste.
- **Chloroplasts** (in plants) – capture sunlight for photosynthesis.

All animal and plant cells, as well as fungi and protists, are eukaryotic.

sections.heading: Comparing Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes
sections.body:
The main differences are the presence of a nucleus and membrane‑bound organelles. Prokaryotes are generally smaller (1–5 µm) and reproduce quickly by binary fission. Eukaryotes are larger (10–100 µm) and have more complex internal structures, allowing specialized functions.

Both cell types share a cell membrane, ribosomes, and DNA, showing the common ancestry of all life.

key_terms.meaning: The set of three statements that describe cells as the basic unit of life and their origin.
A simple cell without a nucleus or membrane‑bound organelles.
A complex cell with a nucleus and many specialized organelles.
Organelle that generates ATP through cellular respiration.
Plant organelle that converts light energy into chemical energy via photosynthesis.
Molecular machine that assembles proteins from amino acids.

quiz.q: Which statement is NOT part of the cell theory?
options: All living things are made of cells.
Cells are the basic unit of structure and function.
All cells come from pre‑existing cells.
quiz.why: Spontaneous generation was disproved; cells arise from existing cells.

quiz.q: What structure holds the DNA in a prokaryotic cell?
quiz.why: Prokaryotes have a nucleoid region, not a membrane‑bound nucleus.

quiz.q: Which organelle is responsible for producing most of the cell’s ATP?
quiz.why: Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.

quiz.q: Which feature distinguishes eukaryotic cells from prokaryotic cells?
quiz.why: Only eukaryotes have a membrane‑bound nucleus.

flashcards.front: What are the three main ideas of cell theory?
flashcards.back: 1) All living things are composed of cells; 2) The cell is the basic unit of life; 3) All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.

flashcards.front: Name two key differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
flashcards.back: Prokaryotes lack a nucleus and membrane‑bound organelles; eukaryotes have both.

flashcards.front: What is the function of the mitochondrion?
flashcards.back: To produce ATP, the cell’s main energy currency, through cellular respiration.

flashcards.front: Where does photosynthesis occur in plant cells?
flashcards.back: In the chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll and convert light energy into chemical energy.

flashcards.front: What role do ribosomes play in the cell?
flashcards.back: Ribosomes synthesize proteins by linking amino acids according to mRNA instructions.
